'''Žarko Dolinar''' (3 July 1920 – 9 March 2003) was a Croatian biologist and table tennis player who won eight medals at the [[World Table Tennis Championships]].<ref>[http://www.ittf.com/ittf_stats/All_events3.asp?ID=1703 "DOLINAR Zarko (YUG) "] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121016155721/http://www.ittf.com/ittf_stats/All_events3.asp?ID=1703 |date=16 October 2012 }}. ITTF Database</ref>

He was born in a family of [[Slovenes|Slovene]] economic migrants to Croatia.<ref>{{cite journal|url=http://www.ceeol.com/aspx/getdocument.aspx?logid=5&id=6c90d3ce-8e89-47ea-bc74-5d0de28734c0 |journal=CEEOL Migration and Ethnic Themes |issue =4 |year=2006|pages=421–445|volume=22|author=Vera Krzisnik Bukic|title=Znameniti Slovenci na Hrvaškem skozi zgodovino}}</ref> In 1939, at the age of 18 he became the national champion of [[Kingdom of Yugoslavia|Yugoslavia]].<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20070504212853/http://www.hsts.hr/history.php Povijest hrvatskog stolnog tenisa (History of Croatian Table Tennis)]. hsts.hr</ref> Dolinar was champion of the [[Independent State of Croatia]] multiple times, and also competed for its national team on nine occasions.<ref>{{cite journal|url=http://www.hkz-kkv.ch/pdf/do93.pdf |title=ŽARKO DOLINAR. 1920 – 2003|journal=Društvene obavijesti|volume=93/94|year=2003|page=11}}</ref>

He also won three [[English Open (table tennis)|English Open]] titles.

Dolinar is [[List of athletes with advanced degrees|one of few world sporting champions with a Ph.D. degree]].<ref name="etthof"/> He graduated from the [[University of Zagreb]] Faculty of Veterinary Medicine in 1949, and received a doctorate in 1959.<ref>[http://www.index.hr/vijesti/clanak/u-83-godini-umro-zarko-dolinar-slavni-stolnotenisac-i-znanstvenik/123691.aspx "U 83. godini umro Žarko Dolinar, slavni stolnotenisač i znanstvenik"]. index.hr</ref> He was world doubles champion with his partner, [[Vilim Harangozo]]. Dolinar was also head of the Sports Science Committee for the [[International Table Tennis Federation]] (ITTF).

A university professor in both [[Zagreb]] and [[Basel]], Dolinar and his brother Boris were honored as the [[Righteous Among the Nations]] for saving Jews during [[World War II]]. On a number of occasions, the Dolinar brothers provided Jews with forged identity documents and travel permits, used their connections to have them released from imprisonment, and helped them travel to safety.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.yadvashem.org/yv/en/exhibitions/righteous-sportsmen/dolinar.asp|title=Boris and Žarko Dolinar|work=yadvashem.org|publisher=[[Yad Vashem]]|accessdate=1 March 2019}}</ref>

In 2016, Dolinar was inducted into the [[European Table Tennis Hall of Fame]].<ref name="etthof">{{cite web|url=http://etthof.org/project/zarko-dolinar/|title=Zarko Dolinar|work=European Table Tennis Hall of Fame|publisher=[[European Table Tennis Union]]|accessdate=1 March 2019}}</ref>
